sophie (support): quick heads-up — acme-corp is seeing a p95 jump and intermittent 502s on /v1/generate since the canary deploy last night. Customer reporting time window 2024-05-12 22:08–22:12 UTC. Can we put together a small shotpack (request ids + minimal curl reproduction + prompt set + concurrency profile) to hand off to sg? :wave:

tim (eng-runtime): yep — need sample request ids, model, and approximate token counts. also which region and whether they hit dedicated or hosted.

sophie (support): org: acme-corp (org_9f3). Model: redwood/gpt-medium-v1 (hosted, prod-us-east). Sample request ids: req_202405122208_abc123, req_202405122210_def456, req_202405122211_ghi789. Token windows ~320–420 (including input+output). Observed pattern: burst of ~70–90 parallel clients for ~45–75s, p95 up from 160ms to ~1.2s, a few 502 responses (~0.6% of requests).

maria (eng-sre): good, can you dump a tiny log snippet and the exact error signature? helps narrow to transport vs runtime.

sophie (support): also saw a couple 401s earlier from the customer immediately after token rotation, but those are separate — focus on latency/502s for now.

tim (eng-runtime): OK — here's a minimal curl reproduction I recommend for the shotpack. Use REPRO_TOKEN with Customer's API key copy, rotate headers to include X-Request-ID from sample ids, and run with a simple concurrency harness (see tiny loop below). This reproduces the same model input size / token profile:

```
# single-shot curl (use for smoke)
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REPRO_TOKEN" \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -H "X-Request-ID: req_repro_{{N}}" \\
  -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-medium-v1","input":"Summarize: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. Repeat to ~300 tokens","max_tokens":256}' \\ 
# small concurrency harness (bash, run for 60s)
for i in {1..80}; do
  (for n in {1..75}; do
     curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
       -H "Authorization: Bearer $REPRO_TOKEN" \\
       -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
       -H "X-Request-ID: req_repro_${i}_${n}" \\
       -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-medium-v1","input":"<PROMPT-PAYLOAD>","max_tokens":256}' &
  done; wait) &
done; wait
```

maria (eng-sre): nice. For the shotpack please include:
- exact prompt set (3 variations) — please paste the real prompt examples (mask any PII)
- concurrency profile: 80 clients, ramp 10s, sustain 60s, ramp-down 5s
- token distribution: 320–420 tokens (attach histogram if available)
- request id list (20 samples)
- a HAR or curl-ids if we need to replay via redwood-playback

sophie (support): assembling now. prompt set (sanitized):
1) "Write a concise product summary for a developer platform that handles model inference and deployment. Keep it ~300 tokens."
2) "Given the following log excerpt, extract error type and recommended next step. Keep output concise."
3) "Compose a polite customer update explaining we're investigating an intermittent latency spike. ~150 tokens."

jason (customer-success): tagging the customer thread — acme has agreed to provide a short time window for us to run stress tests using a masked API key. I'll coordinate schedule (prefer evening PST). :thumbsup:

If we hit 502s locally we can capture a full debug bundle: kernel logs + runtime panics + tenant resource snapshot.

tim (eng-runtime): thumbs up. If you hit asymmetric failures (502s only on some hosts) include `runtime-host` header value from upstream logs so we can isolate instance-level issues.
